blockers.title: The boundedness exception still omits two independently owner-recorded source clauses from its formal scope.
blockers.finding: P-002-4 and P-005-2 each impose their own Journaled/redacted/bounded obligation in an owner-recorded Route-B bound. v5 adds only the file-04 SC-OPS class rule to proposedSupersession.of, and whatIsSuperseded describes only that class-rule displacement. The pre-existing of entries remain labeled as not-a-grant-journal bounds, while the explicit two-displacement text treats P-002-4 only as a containment prohibition and never names either Route-B boundedness clause. Consequently, applying the proposed text would leave at least one reasonable and owner-grounded reading in which both Route-B boundedness obligations survive and conflict with the journal's MUST NOT be dropped or bounded away rule. This is the exact scope ambiguity the frozen v4 findings required v5 to remove, not a request to apply the supersession.
blockers.requiredRepair: Inside the proposed-only SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL text, explicitly add the P-002-4 and P-005-2 Journaled/redacted/bounded clauses to both of and whatIsSuperseded for DR-105 grant-journal bytes only. Align boundednessExceptionOwner with the complete source-owner/concurrence set, including the D-060 operability authority already present in ownersWhoseConcurrenceIsRequired. Preserve every unrelated Route-B clause, reversibility, OPEN standing, and the requirement for a separately authorized reviewed recording plus user-express D-096 (A); do not mint or apply that grant here.

blockers.title: The unbounded append-only journal has no coherent custody, retention, backup, purge, or migration lifecycle.
blockers.finding: The class rule requires durable append-only sequence records with no hard drop bound and fail-close rather than loss. But v5 never discloses whether those records are retained forever, archived, included in backups, restored, migrated, excluded from project purge, or transformed during purge. This is not deferred by the permission candidate: permission-truth-tables.v6 ID-DEP-P5 expressly says those behaviors follow DR-124 closure. It is also not optional under the surviving source text: file 04 and both Route-B bounds require backup/purge scope disclosure, and the live DR-124 row requires custody/backup/purge/migration rules. A project purge can therefore either delete records in violation of the no-drop rule or retain them in violation of an undisclosed purge expectation; the contract gives no adjudication. v5's claim that SCC-V4-B1 is folded is false because that finding expressly required backup/purge/lifecycle consequences.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define the grant journal's exact custody and lifecycle while keeping this artifact candidate-only: retention duration or archival rule; backup inclusion/exclusion and restore behavior; migration handling; project-purge inclusion/exclusion and any tombstone/archive behavior; writer behavior at every loss or capacity boundary; and reversibility consequences. The result must preserve ordering and fail closed without claiming an applied purge/D9 design. If the owners intentionally reserve any property, identify the owning OPEN row and stop claiming DR-124 completeness or full folding of SCC-V4-B1.
